newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU mulls how to prepare east Europeans for euro.
newsitem.headline: EU mulls how to prepare east Europeans for euro.

text.p: The European Commission is considering how best to prepare aspiring European Union members from eastern Europe for joining the single currency.

European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said on Monday that east European applicants could not be treated as "pre-ins" -- EU jargon for the current EU members which will not qualify for the single currency from the start.
But neither could they be left out totally, de Silguy told a conference on Economic and Monetary Union organised by the European Financial Management and Marketing Association (EFMA).
"We are considering a system for membership candidates," de Silguy said. "Maybe we should call them the pre-pre-ins."
He did not elaborate on the system but Commission officials said an exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in which eastern European currencies would be linked to the single currency was not on the cards.
"There is no plan to propose an exchange rate mechanism involving candidate countries," de Silguy's spokesman said.

Most central and eastern European states have applied to join the EU but formal negotiations are not due to start until the Union agrees reforms to its institutions and voting rules currently being negotiated.
The single currency, the euro, is to be introduced in January 1999 in EU states that meet tough budget deficit and debt criteria.
